definition: A cause is in act virtually, or eminently, in a perfection when it has it in a higher way, as a power to produce it, without having it in the same form: whatever perfection is in the effect is in the effective cause 'univocally or more eminently' (ST I q.4 a.2).
note: Lean: a primitive parameter of the sense-fork frame (its own declaration, distinct from the other senses of its disambiguation); it carries no definitional body.
